newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha to form Turkish motorbike venture.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha to form Turkish motorbike venture.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to set up a joint venture in Istanbul to produce and sell motorcycles from January 1, 1997.

The new company, named Beldeyama A.S. and capitalised at $13 million, will be 80 percent owned by Beldesan, the import agent for Yamaha motorcycles, and 20 percent by Yamaha Motor Europe N.V., Yamaha's European unit.
Beldesan also produces and exports moped engines and scooter engine parts for Yamaha's French unit.
Sales of Yamaha's motorcycles in Turkey stand at around 600 units per year. Overall demand for motorcycles in Turkey is running at about 50,000 units per year.
The joint venture has yet to complete details, but is likely to assemble Yamaha's 100 to 125cc motorcycles at an annual rate of about 1,000 units.

In July this year, Istanbul-based Honda Anadolumotorsiklet Uretim Ve Pazarlama A.S., owned 51 percent by Honda Motor Co Ltd, began assembling motorcycles with an annual production capacity of 3,000 units.
